title: The scrubber board's atmospheric guard: what it protects, on what it decides, every number with its source
source: SCRUBBER_SAFETY_SCENARIO.md (Guillaume, 2026-10-11): the safety invariants are atmospheric (CO2 partial pressure within the approved envelope, a forecast that preserves the recovery margin, the sensor fresh and valid, the restart verified, an independent monitor active); the motor's speed is a command, not an invariant. Simulated on the stub board first (slots/scrubber/atmosphere.ts), to be ported to the real board. Oxygen left out on Guillaume's word the same day: the scrubber's business is the CO2.
rules: A software stop is bounded: it names its minutes (at most stop.maxMinutes); an unbounded power off is refused.

A stop or a lower speed is accepted only when the sensor is fresh and valid, the pressure is within its bounds, the forecast is available, the restart is available with its energy reserved (a stop), the CO2 partial pressure is below the warning line now, and the forecast peak (the stop, the restart latency, the recovery) stays below the warning line minus the recovery margin.

The forecast is the board's own: the CO2 emission is estimated from its last readings (what entered the cabin = the rise + what the scrubber removed + what leaked), never from what anyone says about the crew.

During a stop the board restarts on its own: at the end of the bound (back to the speed before the stop), or at once at full speed when the restart margin is lost (restarting now would peak above the warning line minus the margin), when the sensor goes stale or invalid, or when the pressure leaves its bounds.
At or above the limit, full speed is forced and no reduction is accepted, whoever asks.
A restart that fails raises the alarm RESTART FAILED: the board has no other removal; the crew is the escalation.

pressureKpa.status: simulated: a constant sensor on the stub
pressureKpa.note: ppCO2 = ppm x 1e-6 x P; a limit in mmHg is only right for the pressure it was written for (nasa-co2-limits)

warningPpCo2Mmhg.source: docs/library/nasa-co2-limits.md: ELEVATED at 3500 ppm is about 2.7 mmHg at 101.3 kPa
warningPpCo2Mmhg.note: the line a stop may not cross; the cabin leaves NOMINAL above it

limitPpCo2Mmhg.source: docs/library/nasa-co2-limits.md [V2 6004]: the one-hour limit, 3 mmHg (CRITICAL at 4000 ppm)
limitPpCo2Mmhg.note: at or above it the board forces full speed

recoveryMarginMmhg.source: assumption, about 130 ppm at 101.3 kPa, twice the CO2 sensor's accuracy at 2000 ppm (station-topology: 30 ppm + 3 %)
recoveryMarginMmhg.status: to review: needs an engineering approval
recoveryMarginMmhg.note: the forecast peak of a stop stays at least this far under the warning line

sensorMaxAgeSeconds.source: lib/cabin-co2.ts: the board holds a reading for 5 s
sensorMaxAgeSeconds.note: older than this the reading is stale

pressureMinKpa.note: a pressure out of bounds means the limits in mmHg no longer read as written

stopMaxMinutes.note: the longest bound a stop may name

forecastHorizonMinutes.note: how far the board looks for the peak of a lower speed

emissionWindowMinutes.note: the readings the emission estimate averages; fewer valid ones and the forecast is unavailable

restartLatency: specs/cabin-parameters.json, scrubber.restartLatencyMinutes: a property of the scrubber, which the twin reads too
